title: Private Autotune Safety Harness: offline recommendation verifier and policy-backed rollback
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Problem: Customers running Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) want automated batching/caching/quantization suggestions that reduce unit cost but cannot tolerate silent regressions or telemetry leakage. Offline/autotune tooling must run in customer-controlled environments, respect policy gates, and ensure safe staged application with a robust rollback path.

Goal: Deliver an autotune safety harness that can generate recommendations offline (no outbound telemetry), verify expected latency/cost behavior via replay/sim, surface conservative default profiles, and provide a staged, policy-enforced apply/rollback flow suitable for VPC and air-gapped on-prem deployments.

Scope:
- Recommendation generator producing batching and cache policies and suggested quantization profiles.
- Local replay/simulation runner that consumes recent request traces (or synthetic workloads) to estimate latency and throughput impact.
- Policy engine that enforces org rules (max batch size, pinned models, CPU/GPU caps) and flags disallowed changes.
- Staged apply flow: dry-run, canary within private capacity, full apply with safety timer and automated rollback triggers.
- Audit logs and signed change artifacts for offline compliance reviews.

Out of scope for this ticket: telemetry collection from customer networks, model re-training, or interactive UI polish.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Recommendation generator produces deterministic JSON recommendation artifacts that contain batching, cache TTL, and quantization suggestions for a given workload trace.
A2: Replay runner consumes a record-format trace and returns cost/latency delta estimates within +/-20% of real measurements in our internal benchmarks.
A3: Policy engine rejects any recommendation that violates configured org policies; rejections include a human-readable reason code.
A4: Staged apply implements dry-run -> canary (10% capacity) -> full apply with automatic rollback on defined SLO regressions (latency or error-rate).
A5: All actions emit signed audit artifacts (GPG or local HSM signature) stored alongside recommendations for offline review.
A6: No external network call is required to run recommendation generation or verification in Private mode (validated via offline test harness).
design_notes: Use recommendation artifacts (JSON) that include: profile_version, deterministic seed, workload_summary, suggestions with rationale and estimated token savings.

Replay runner will be implemented as a local binary that uses the same batching and KV-cache logic as the serving runtime to ensure comparable results; it runs entirely on customer infrastructure and accepts compressed traces.

Policy engine will be rule-driven (YAML) with ordered checks: security (no KMS ops), resource caps (max_batch, max_seq_len), and model-compat checks (quantization compatibility list). Rules must be editable by customers and supported by Redwood defaults.
For signing artifacts we will support both GPG and an HSM-backed signer for on-prem. If HSM not available, fail open to manual approval path but mark artifacts accordingly.
Trade-offs: conservative defaults reduce cost savings but increase safety. We will expose a two-tier mode: conservative (default) and aggressive (explicit opt-in with elevated approvals).
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal dry-run in staging with synthetic traces (team-only).
Phase 1: alpha with 3 pilot customers under NDA; enable offline mode and collect signed artifacts for manual validation.
Phase 2: beta with limited self-serve in Private console; include policy templates and RBAC guardrails.
Phase 3: general availability after two pilot customers complete 4-week validation and security signoff.
test_plan: Unit tests for recommendation generator determinism and schema validation.
Integration tests of replay runner against the serving runtime in CI with small synthetic datasets.
Golden-file comparisons for cost/latency estimates; tolerances recorded in test metadata.
Offline-mode E2E test: run full flow (generate -> replay -> policy -> sign) in an isolated VM with no outbound network and verify no calls to external endpoints.
Canary failure injection tests: deliberately degrade backend to verify rollback triggers.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Replay mismatch with production behavior could lead to bad recommendations. Mitigation: use same runtime code-paths for batching/cache in replay and add a calibration step using a small live canary.
Risk: Policy gaps allow unsafe changes. Mitigation: provide conservative default rule-set and require manager approval for any rule relaxations.
Risk: Customers without HSM can't sign artifacts securely. Mitigation: offer manual out-of-band approval workflow and clearly label unsigned artifacts.
Risk: Large traces are expensive to replay. Mitigation: provide trace sampling utilities and delta sampling to focus on recent traffic patterns.
